issues.text: Unlisted claim, and not true of stage-0 code. The split did more than make existing dependencies visible: PlaceOrderLong computes the discount inline (PlaceOrderLong.cs:26 `totalVnd -= totalVnd * 10 / 100;`) and never mentions NamingAfter, while PlaceOrderSplit.cs:29 calls `NamingAfter.TotalVnd`. The cross-class dependency the lesson centres on was added by the split. Also, in PlaceOrderLong the checks and the email line never touched the shared variable (claim 9), so not every dependency was 'a shared variable'.
issues.quote: it did not reduce how much `Place` depends on — it only made those dependencies visible as calls instead of a shared variable
issues.fix: Replace with: 'it did not reduce how much `Place` depends on — `Place` now calls each job by name, and pricing now depends on another class, `NamingAfter`.' Add a claim: 'PlaceOrderLong computes the discount inline (line 26) and does not reference NamingAfter; PlaceOrderSplit.TotalWithShippingVnd calls NamingAfter.TotalVnd (line 29).'

issues.text: 'still arrive from outside' implies changes arrived from another file before the split too; in PlaceOrderLong the discount lives in the same method (PlaceOrderLong.cs:26). §8 Connections already says the effect is 'now crossing from one class to another'.
issues.quote: why do changes still land here — and still arrive from outside?
issues.fix: Replace with: 'why do changes still land here — and now arrive from outside too?'

issues.fix: Name each half: 'Measured method by method, cohesion is high; measured as a class, it is still low, because the class holds all four jobs. And coupling did not drop: `Place` still has an arrow to each of them.'
